A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CausVid and provide readable main text, equations, algorithms, figures, tables, and supplementary material. The shorter v4 reflects layout reflow rather than missing material.

before.justification: v3 reports original video-generation evaluations, efficiency measurements, ablations, a human preference study, and appendix VBench-Long results.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results, including the benchmark tables, human preference study, and supplementary evaluations.

M1.justification: Sections 4.1–4.4 and Algorithms 1–2 retain the same causal transformer, ODE initialization, asymmetric DMD training, and KV-cached inference. Figure 5's reformatting does not change the architecture.

E1.justification: Training data and evaluation coverage are unchanged: short and long text-to-video generation, image-to-video generation, streaming translation, and dynamic prompting. Both retain the 946-prompt VBench-Long evaluation and 14-minute example.

E2.justification: Tables 1–7 and Figures 7–8 retain the same comparators within each experiment, including StreamV2V in Table 5 and the same seven leaderboard comparators in Table 7.

E3.justification: Resolution, frame rate, inference schedule, training budgets, metrics, and evaluation samples remain unchanged. The human study still uses 29 prompts and three ratings per prompt and model pair, totaling 87 ratings per pair.

E4.justification: Table 4 retains the initialization and teacher-choice ablations. Figure 8's error-accumulation analysis and Figure 9's 14-minute example are unchanged; renaming Section 5.4 introduces no new analysis.

E5.justification: Both specify a fixed random seed of zero for human-study videos and use the same statistical reporting practices. v4 adds no repeated-run information, uncertainty estimates, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Tables 1–7, Figure 7's preference percentages, Figure 8's curves, and the qualitative examples retain the same results. CausVid still reports 1.3-second latency, 9.4 FPS throughput, and a VBench-Long total score of 84.27.

T1.justification: Equations 1–6, including the DMD gradient, causal attention mask, and initialization loss, are mathematically unchanged. No formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or removed.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and discussion retain the same contributions and claims concerning asymmetric distillation, video quality, reduced error accumulation, streaming speed, and zero-shot applications. Novelty and performance claims are unchanged.

C2.justification: The explanations of teacher-related error accumulation and the qualifications concerning long-video degradation, temporal flickering, reduced diversity, VAE-imposed latency, and throughput limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Both disclose the same preprocessing, hyperparameters, 1000 ODE pairs, 3000 initialization iterations, 6000 distillation iterations, and approximately two days on 64 H100 GPUs. Code/model release statements and access information are unchanged.

R1.justification: Both retain the same 112 cited works and research positioning. Bibliography back-reference page numbers change because material reflows, without adding or removing cited research.

P1.justification: Section 5.4 is renamed from 'Extremely Long Video Generation' to 'Ultra-Long Video Generation.' The prose and section sequence otherwise remain essentially identical.

P2.justification: Figure 5 has revised typography and compact, single-line frame labels. Figure 7 moves from PDF page 10 to page 9, tables shift within pages 10–11, and references and supplementary pages reflow. No figures or tables are added or removed.

improvement.justification: v4 tidies Figure 5, renames Section 5.4, and reflows existing material. These cosmetic refinements leave the scientific explanations, empirical support, reproducibility information, and acknowledged limitations essentially unchanged, producing no meaningful net difference in overall quality.
